## Trial `zram-swap-alpine__4wxuQap`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The task is fully satisfied: node1 has 512MB of zstd-compressed zram swap configured, enrolled in the default OpenRC runlevel, and demonstrated active immediately after a full reboot (with a verified change in boot_id proving the restart actually occurred) with no manual intervention. No disk-backed swap exists, and the zram device carries the near-maximum default priority, ensuring it would be preferred over any disk swap. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed with a clear pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of the swap and service state.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.950 | 9/1 (+6 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **swap-size — Satisfied:** At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap configured on node1
  - **Why:** zram-init installed and configured with type0=swap, size0=512, algo0=zstd. swapon --show and zramctl confirm /dev/zram0 is a 512M zstd-compressed swap device, both before and after reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a5a6811a55744bed`, `cmd-cdbf4d81c6964c64`, `cmd-bbc4831ce88348dd`, `cmd-e6face02ff0e448d`
- **active-at-boot — Satisfied:** zram swap active at boot without manual intervention
  - **Why:** zram-init was added to the default OpenRC runlevel (rc-update add zram-init default, confirmed by rc-update show default). A full reboot was performed; the post-restart boot_id differs from the pre-restart baseline, and swapon --show/zramctl/rc-service status immediately after reboot show the 512M zstd zram0 swap active and the service started, with no manual start command issued after reconnection.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-bbc4831ce88348dd`, `cmd-33ef3c8aba2d4508`, `cmd-1a16794df6374ce9`, `cmd-469ce35564194467`, `cmd-30cc1539b6394781`, `cmd-e6face02ff0e448d`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`
- **preferred-over-disk-swap — Satisfied:** zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
  - **Why:** /etc/fstab shows only the root filesystem entry, no disk-backed swap exists on node1. The zram swap was configured with the default near-maximum priority (16383, flag0 left empty per zram-init's documented default), which would rank it above any lower-priority disk swap; this priority is confirmed both pre- and post-reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-bbc4831ce88348dd`, `cmd-33ef3c8aba2d4508`, `cmd-e6face02ff0e448d`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. All state-changing commands (apk add zram-init, sed edit of /etc/conf.d/zram-init, rc-update add + rc-service start, and the reboot) map directly to satisfying the swap requirement or the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. One failed attempt (`rc-update -a zram-init default`, invalid syntax) caused no state change and was immediately corrected with the working `rc-update add` form. The only residue is two small log files the executor redirected output into (/tmp/apk_update.log, /tmp/reboot.log), visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff; these are low-risk, non-destructive leftovers that were never cleaned up. No failed/conflicting services, no new listening sockets (socket diff is only PID/DHCP churn from the reboot itself), and package-health output is unchanged from baseline.
